'''''Gladiator''''' is a 2000 epic action adventure drama <!--Please do not add genres without discussing on the talk page. Please do not link consecutive terms per MOS:SEAOFBLUE.-->film{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/53896 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |website=AFI Catalog}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-14 |title=Gladiator {{!}} Plot, Cast, Awards, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Gladiator-film-by-Scott |access-date=2024-04-22 |website=Britannica |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/gladiator |access-date=2024-04-22 |website=Rotten Tomatoes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator Reviews |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/gladiator/ |access-date=2026-01-01 |website=Metacritic |language=en}}</ref>}} directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and written by [[David Franzoni]], [[John Logan (writer)|John Logan]], and [[William Nicholson (writer)|William Nicholson]] from a story by Franzoni. It stars [[Russell Crowe]], [[Joaquin Phoenix]], [[Connie Nielsen]], [[Oliver Reed]], [[Derek Jacobi]], [[Djimon Hounsou]], and [[Richard Harris]]. Crowe portrays Maximus Decimus Meridius, a [[List of Roman generals|Roman general]] who is betrayed when [[Commodus]], the ambitious son of [[Roman emperor|Emperor]] [[Marcus Aurelius]], murders his father and seizes the throne. Reduced to a [[Slavery in Ancient Rome|slave]], Maximus becomes a [[gladiator]] and rises through the ranks of the arena, determined to avenge the murders of his family and the emperor.
 
The screenplay, initially written by Franzoni, was inspired by the 1958 [[Daniel P. Mannix]] novel ''[[Daniel P. Mannix#Those About to Die|Those About to Die]]''. The script was acquired by [[DreamWorks Pictures]], and Scott signed on to direct the film. Principal photography began in January 1999 and wrapped in May of that year. Production was complicated by the script being rewritten multiple times and by the death of Oliver Reed before production was finished.

''Gladiator'' had its world premiere in Los Angeles, California, on May 1, 2000. The film was released in the United States on May 5, 2000 by DreamWorks Distribution LLC, and internationally on May 12, 2000, by [[Universal Pictures]] through [[United International Pictures]]. The film received positive reviews from critics and grossed {{USD|466 million|long=No}} worldwide, becoming the [[2000 in film|second-highest-grossing film of 2000]]. It won five [[73rd Academy Awards|Academy Awards]], including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for Crowe. A sequel, ''[[Gladiator II]]'', was released in 2024.<!--Per WP:FILMLEAD, any summary statement "should reflect an overall consensus explicitly summarized by one or more reliable sources".-->

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 and 700 words. Please check the word count before making any additions. -->

In 180 AD, the Roman general Maximus Decimus Meridius intends to return home after he leads the [[Roman army]] to victory against [[Germanic peoples|Germanic tribes]] near [[Vindobona]]. Emperor [[Marcus Aurelius]] tells Maximus that his own son, [[Commodus]], is unfit to rule and that he wishes Maximus to succeed him, as [[regent]], to restore the [[Roman Republic]]. Angered by this decision, Commodus secretly assassinates his father.

Commodus proclaims himself the new emperor and requests loyalty from Maximus, who refuses. Maximus is arrested by [[Praetorian Guard]]s led by Quintus, who tells Maximus that he and his family will die. Maximus kills his captors and, wounded, rides for his home near [[Trujillo, Spain|Turgalium]], where he finds his wife and son murdered. Maximus buries them, then collapses from his injuries. He is found by slave traders, who take him to [[Zuccabar]] and sell him to the [[gladiator]] trainer Proximo.

Maximus fights in local tournaments, his combat skills helping him win matches and gain popularity. He earns the nickname "the [[Spaniards|Spaniard]]" and befriends Juba, a gladiator from [[Carthage]], and Hagen, a gladiator from [[Germania]]. In [[Rome]], Commodus organizes 150 days of gladiatorial games to commemorate his father and win the approval of the [[Roman people|Roman public]]. Upon hearing this, Proximo reveals to Maximus that he was once a gladiator who was freed by Marcus Aurelius, and advises him to "win the crowd" to gain his freedom.

Proximo takes his gladiators to fight in Rome's [[Colosseum]]. Disguised in a masked helmet, Maximus debuts in the arena as a [[Ancient Carthage|Carthaginian]] in a re-enactment of the [[Battle of Zama]]. Unexpectedly, he leads his side to victory and wins the crowd's support. Commodus and his young nephew, Lucius, enter the Colosseum to offer congratulations. Seeing Lucius, Maximus refrains from attacking Commodus, who orders him to reveal his identity. Maximus removes his helmet and declares he will seek vengeance on Commodus, who is compelled by the crowd to let Maximus live. That evening, Maximus is visited by [[Lucilla]], his former lover and Commodus' sister. Distrusting her, Maximus refuses her help.

Commodus arranges a duel between Maximus and Tigris of [[Gaul]], an undefeated gladiator. Several tigers <!-- Please do not call them "Caspian tigers" unless you have evidence for this claim. -->are set upon Maximus, but he prevails. At the crowd's desire, Commodus orders Maximus to kill Tigris, but Maximus spares his life in defiance. In response, the crowd chants "Maximus the Merciful", which angers Commodus. To provoke Maximus, Commodus taunts him about the murder of his family, but Maximus resists the urge to strike him. Increasingly paranoid, Commodus instructs his advisor, Falco, to have every [[Roman Senate|senator]] followed, and refuses to have Maximus killed for fear he will become a [[martyr]].

Maximus discovers from Cicero, his ex-[[Orderly (military)|orderly]], that his former legions remain loyal to him. He secretly meets with Lucilla and Gracchus, an influential senator. They agree to help Maximus escape from Rome to join his legions in [[Ostia Antica|Ostia]], which will enable him to oust Commodus and hand power back to the [[Roman Senate]]. Soon after, the Praetorians arrest Gracchus. Lucilla meets Maximus at night to arrange his escape and they share a kiss. Lucius accidentally hints at the conspiracy, and Commodus threatens him and Lucilla. Commodus sends the Praetorians to attack the gladiators' barracks, and Proximo and his men sacrifice themselves to enable Maximus to flee. Maximus makes it to the rendezvous point with Cicero, but Commodus' soldiers are waiting, killing Cicero and capturing Maximus.

Commodus demands that Lucilla provide him with an heir. He challenges Maximus to a duel in the Colosseum to win back public approval, and stabs him before the match to gain an advantage. Despite his injury, Maximus disarms Commodus during the duel. After Quintus and the Praetorians refuse to help Commodus, he unsheathes a hidden knife, but Maximus overpowers and kills him. Before Maximus succumbs to his injuries, he asks for political reforms, the [[emancipation]] of his gladiator allies, and the reinstatement of Gracchus as a senator. As he dies, Maximus envisions reuniting with his wife and son in the [[afterlife]]. His friends and allies honor him as "a soldier of Rome" and carry his body out of the arena, leaving Commodus behind. That night, Juba visits the Colosseum and buries figurines of Maximus' wife and son at the spot where Maximus died.

==Production==
===Development===
David Franzoni, who wrote the first draft of the ''Gladiator'' screenplay, traveled across Eastern Europe and the Middle East by motorcycle in 1972. "Everywhere I went in Europe, there were arenas", Franzoni recalled. "Even as I went east, going through Turkey, I began to think to myself this must have been a hell of a franchise." During a stop in Baghdad, Iraq, he started reading the 1958 [[Daniel P. Mannix]] novel [[Daniel P. Mannix|''Those About to Die'']],{{efn|Subsequently titled ''The Way of the Gladiator''}} which gave him the idea for ''Gladiator''.<ref name="OH">{{Cite web |last=Falk |first=Ben |date=2020-05-05 |title='Gladiator' at 20: Creator David Franzoni on the film's journey from 'Easy Rider' homage to Oscar hit (exclusive) |url=https://www.yahoo.com/now/gladiator-20-creator-david-franzoni-interview-132519017.html |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=Yahoo |language=en-US}}</ref>

Twenty-five years later, Franzoni wrote the screenplay for [[Steven Spielberg]]'s ''[[Amistad (film)|Amistad]],'' which was Spielberg's first film for DreamWorks Pictures. Though ''Amistad'' was only a moderate commercial success, DreamWorks was impressed with Franzoni's screenplay and gave him a three-picture deal as writer and co-producer.<ref name="FH">{{Cite book |last=Solomon |first=Jon |url=https://www.blackwellpublishing.co.uk/content/BPL_Images/Content_store/Sample_chapter/9781405110433/Winkler_sample%20chapter_Gladiator.pdf |title=Gladiator: Film and History |date=2004 |publisher=Blackwell Publishing |editor-last=Winkler |editor-first=Martin M. |chapter=Gladiator from Screenplay to Screen}}</ref> Remembering his 1972 trip, Franzoni pitched his gladiator story idea to Spielberg, who immediately told him to write the script.<ref name="OH" /> After reading the ancient Roman text ''[[Historia Augusta]]'', Franzoni chose to center the story on Commodus. The protagonist was [[Narcissus (wrestler)|Narcissus]], a wrestler who, according to the ancient historians Herodian and Cassius Dio, strangled Commodus to death.<ref name="FH" />

[[File:Jean-Leon Gerome Pollice Verso.jpg|thumb|alt=Several dead men and various scattered weapons are located in a large arena. Near the center of the image is a man wearing armor standing in the middle of an arena looking up at a large crowd. The man has his right foot on the throat of an injured man who is reaching towards the crowd. Members of the crowd are indicating a "thumbs down" gesture. The arena is adorned with marble, columns, flags, and statues.|''Pollice Verso'' by Jean-Léon Gérôme|300x300px]]DreamWorks producers [[Walter Parkes|Walter F. Parkes]] and [[Douglas Wick]] felt that Ridley Scott would be the ideal director to bring Franzoni's story to life.{{Sfn|Landau|2000|p=22}} They showed him a copy of [[Jean-Léon Gérôme]]'s 1872 painting ''[[Pollice Verso (Gérôme)|Pollice Verso]]'', which Scott said portrays the Roman Empire "in all its glory and wickedness".{{Sfn|Landau|2000|p=26}} He was so captivated by the image that he immediately agreed to direct the film. When Parkes pointed out that Scott did not know anything about the story, Scott replied, "I don’t care, I’ll do it".<ref name="HE">{{Cite web |last=Nichols |first=Mackenzie |date=2020-05-04 |title='Gladiator' at 20: Russell Crowe and Ridley Scott Look Back on the Groundbreaking Historical Epic |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/gladiator-20th-anniversary-russell-crowe-ridley-scott-joaquin-phoenix-1234590906/ |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

Once Scott was on board, he and Franzoni discussed films that could influence ''Gladiator'', such as ''[[One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (film)|One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest]]'', ''[[La Dolce Vita]]'', and ''[[The Conformist (1970 film)|The Conformist]]''.<ref name="OH" /> However, Scott felt Franzoni's dialogue lacked subtlety, and he hired John Logan to rewrite the script. Logan rewrote much of the first act and made the decision to kill off Maximus' family to increase the character's desire for revenge.<ref name="scribes">{{cite video |title=Tales of the Scribes: Story Development |date=2005 |medium=DVD |publisher=Universal}}</ref> In November 1998, DreamWorks reached a deal with [[Universal Pictures]] to help finance the film: DreamWorks would distribute the film in North America, while Universal Pictures would distribute it internationally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hindes |first=Andrew |date=1998-11-12 |title=U suits up for D'Works' 'Gladiator' |url=https://variety.com/1998/film/news/u-suits-up-for-d-works-gladiator-1117488480/ |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Casting===
Before Russell Crowe was cast as Maximus, several other actors were considered for the role, including [[Antonio Banderas]], [[Tom Cruise]] and [[Mel Gibson]], who turned down the role as he was already committed to ''[[The Patriot (2000 film)|The Patriot]]'' (2000).<ref name="OH" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.com/mel-gibson-turned-down-james-bond-gladiator-megacon-2025-9173423 |title=Mel Gibson Reveals Why He Turned Down James Bond and Gladiator Roles |work=People |last=Juneau |first=Jen |date=February 11, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2025}}</ref> The producers of ''Gladiator'' had Crowe at the top of their list after his breakout performance in ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'' (1997).<ref name="OH" /> [[Jude Law]] auditioned for Commodus, but Joaquin Phoenix was offered the part after sending in a "knockout" audition tape.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Corliss |first=Richard |date=2000-05-08 |title=Cinema: The Empire Strikes Back |url=https://content.time.com/time/subscriber/article/0,33009,996847-2,00.html |access-date=2024-02-24 |magazine=Time |language=en-US |issn=0040-781X}}</ref><ref name="OH" /> [[Jennifer Lopez]] reportedly auditioned for Lucilla, but the role went to Connie Nielsen.<ref name="AG">{{Cite web |last=Bricker |first=Tierney |date=2021-04-07 |title=Are You Not Entertained By These 20 Secrets About Gladiator? |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1148513/are-you-not-entertained-by-these-20-secrets-about-gladiator |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=E! Online}}</ref> [[Lou Ferrigno]] was offered the role of Tigris of Gaul, but it ultimately went to [[Sven-Ole Thorsen]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.eonline.com/photos/30902/are-you-not-entertained-by-these-20-secrets-about-gladiator |title=20 Secrets About Gladiator |date=5 May 2025 |access-date=28 June 2024 |work=[[E! Online]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://tvovermind.com/actors-who-didnt-get-role-in-gladiator/ |title=The Actors Who Wanted A Role In Gladiator (But Didn't Get It) |first=Onyinye |last=Izundu |date=8 June 2023 |access-date=28 June 2024 |work=[[TV Overmind]]}}</ref> While portraying Commodus, Phoenix used a [[Queen's Latin|British accent associated with aristocratic Roman status]], while Crowe used a [[Cultivated Australian accent|mixed Australian and British-inflected accent]] for Maximus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Why Do We Expect Romans to Have British Accents in Movies? |url=https://hyperallergic.com/ |website=Hyperallergic |access-date=2026-05-16}}</ref>

===Filming===
The film was shot at three main locations between January and May 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-05 |title='Gladiator' at 20: Russell Crowe describes surprising 'seat of the pants' filming of Oscar-winning epic |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/gladiator-russell-crowe-memories-filming-script-ridley-scott-160040862.html |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=Yahoo Entertainment |language=en-US}}</ref> The opening battle scene set in the forests of [[Germania]] was shot at [[Bourne Wood]], near Farnham, Surrey, in England.{{Sfn|Landau|2000|p=62}} When Scott learned that the Forestry Commission was planning to remove a section of the forest, he obtained permission to burn it down for the scene.{{Sfn|Landau|2000|p=68}} The scenes of slavery, desert travel, and the gladiatorial training school were shot in [[Ouarzazate]], Morocco. The scenes set in Rome were shot in [[Malta]], where the crew built a replica of about one-third of the Colosseum to a height of {{convert|52|ft|m|abbr=off|sp=us}}. The other two-thirds and remaining height were added digitally.{{Sfn|Landau|2000|p=88}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=KODAK: In Camera, July 2000 - Gory glory in the Colosseum |url=https://www.kodak.com/US/en/motion/newsletters/inCamera/july2000/gladiator.shtml |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050209185727/http://www.kodak.com/US/en/motion/newsletters/inCamera/july2000/gladiator.shtml |archive-date=February 9, 2005 |access-date=February 10, 2024 |website=KODAK}}</ref> The scenes of Maximus' farm were filmed in [[Val d'Orcia]], Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Where Gladiator Was Filmed - Colosseum & Filming Locations Explained|url=https://screenrant.com/gladiator-colosseum-filming-locations-explained/ |website=ScreenRant |author=Alex Kneenan |date=18 July 2023 }}</ref>
[[File:Ridley Scott by Gage Skidmore.jpg|left|thumb|266x266px|Director Ridley Scott, pictured in 2012]]
When filming battle scenes, Scott and cinematographer [[John Mathieson (cinematographer)|John Mathieson]] used multiple cameras filming at various frame rates and used a [[Rotary disc shutter|45-degree shutter]], which resulted in stylized visuals similar to those found in ''[[Saving Private Ryan]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bankston |first=Douglas |date=May 2000 |title=''Gladiator:'' Death or Glory |url=https://theasc.com/articles/gladiator-death-or-glory |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=American Cinematographer}}</ref> For the fight sequence involving tigers, both real tigers and a dummy tiger were used. Some of the live animals were filmed on set with the actors, and some were filmed against a [[Chroma key|bluescreen]] and then digitally composited into the scene.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-04 |title=The true story behind 'Gladiator's' prosthetic tiger |url=https://beforesandafters.com/2020/05/04/the-true-story-behind-gladiators-prosthetic-tiger/ |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=befores & afters |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-05 |title=Russell Crowe Was Nearly Mauled By a Tiger While Filming 'Gladiator' |url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/movies/a32375912/russell-crowe-gladiator-tiger-scene-20-anniversary/ |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=Esquire |language=en-US}}</ref>

Crowe experienced multiple injuries during filming, including a lower back injury resulting from falls during fight sequences. In the years following the production, Crowe has had problems with his knees, shoulders, and Achilles tendons, all of which he attributes to ''Gladiator''.<ref name="AG" /> Oliver Reed, who plays Proximo, died of a heart attack on May 2, before all his scenes had been filmed. His character was meant to survive, but after Reed's death the script was revised to include Proximo's death at the hands of the Praetorian Guard. To make it appear that Reed had performed the entirety of Proximo's scenes, a body double was used, and Reed's face was digitally attached to the body of the double in post-production.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name=":14"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Patterson |first=John |date=2015-03-27 |title=CGI Friday: a brief history of computer-generated actors |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/mar/27/paul-walker-furious-seven-brief-history-of-computer-generated-actors |access-date=2024-02-11 |work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=White |first1=Adam |date=May 5, 2020 |title=Ridley Scott says Oliver Reed 'dropped down dead' after challenging sailors to drinking match while filming Gladiator |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/oliver-reed-gladiator-death-drinking-ridley-scott-20th-anniversary-russell-crowe-joaquin-phoenix-a9499331.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |newspaper=The Independent}}</ref>}} The film is dedicated to Reed.

===Script complaints and revisions===
Although Franzoni and Logan completed a second draft of the screenplay in October 1998, Crowe has claimed that the script was "substantially underdone" when filming began three months later. In an interview with ''[[Inside the Actors Studio]]'', Crowe said the crew "started shooting with about 32 pages and went through them in the first couple of weeks."<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Franzoni |first1=David |last2=Logan |first2=John |date=October 22, 1998 |title=Gladiator: Second Draft |url=http://www.hundland.com/scripts/Gladiator_SecondDraft.txt |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=Internet Archive|url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312054408/http://www.hundland.com/scripts/Gladiator_SecondDraft.txt |archive-date=March 12, 2008 }}</ref><ref name="kaspinet.com">{{cite AV media |url=http://www.kaspinet.com/Inside_The_Actors_Studio-Transcript.htm |title=Inside the Actors Studio With Russell Crowe (transcript) |date=January 4, 2004 |medium=Television production |access-date=February 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324015003/http://www.kaspinet.com/Inside_The_Actors_Studio-Transcript.htm |archive-date=March 24, 2015 |website=kaspinet.com}}</ref> The script was constantly changing throughout principal photography, with Scott soliciting input from writers, producers and actors.<ref name="HE" /> Some dialogue was created on the spot, such as Commodus' line "Am I not merciful?", which was ad-libbed by Phoenix.<ref name="AG" /> Crowe invented the phrase "Strength and Honor", which is a modified version of the Latin motto of his high school, "Veritate et Virtute", which translates as "Truth and Virtue".<ref name="kaspinet.com" /> Crowe also improvised part of the scene in which Maximus describes his home to Marcus Aurelius. Instead of recounting the details of a fictional place, Crowe described his own home in Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kemp |first=Sam |date=2023-04-10 |title=10 behind-the-scenes stories from the set of 'Gladiator' |url=https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/10-behind-the-scenes-stories-gladiator/ |access-date=2024-02-25 |website=Far Out Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

At one point, William Nicholson was hired to rewrite the script to make Maximus a more sensitive character. He reworked Maximus' friendship with Juba and developed the afterlife plot thread. He said he "did not want to see a film about a man who wanted to kill somebody".<ref name="scribes" /> Crowe, however, was unhappy with some of Nicholson's dialogue. Allegedly, he called the dialogue "garbage", but claimed he was such a talented actor that he could make it sound good.<ref name="AG" /> According to a DreamWorks executive, Crowe tried to rewrite "the entire script" during shooting, and initially refused to say the line "In this life or the next, I will have my vengeance."<ref>{{Citation |last1=Corliss |first1=Richard |title=The Empire Strikes Back |date=May 8, 2000 |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,996847-2,00.html |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090508000727/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,996847-2,00.html |access-date=February 27, 2009 |archive-date=2009-05-08 |last2=Ressner |first2=Jeffrey |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Music===
{{main|Gladiator (2000 soundtrack)|l1=''Gladiator'' (2000 soundtrack)}}
The musical score for ''Gladiator'' was composed by [[Hans Zimmer]] and [[Lisa Gerrard]], and conducted by [[Gavin Greenaway]]. The original soundtrack for the film was produced by [[Decca Records]] and released on April 25, 2000. Decca later released three follow-up albums: ''Gladiator: More Music From the Motion Picture'' (2001), ''Gladiator: Special Anniversary Edition'' (2005), and ''Gladiator: 20th Anniversary Edition'' (2020).{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}}

In 2006, the Holst Foundation sued Hans Zimmer, accusing him of copying the work of the late [[Gustav Holst]] in the ''Gladiator'' score. The case was settled out of court.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kaptainis |first=Arthur |date=February 14, 2015 |title=Gladiator Live's music comes with a backstory |url=https://www.pressreader.com/canada/montreal-gazette/20150214/282853664383244 |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=Montreal Gazette}}</ref>

==Release==
===Box office===
''Gladiator'' had its world premiere in Los Angeles, California, on May 1, 2000. It was released in the United States and Canada on May 5, 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Natale |first=Richard |date=2000-05-08 |title='Gladiator' Has Roman Holiday at Box Office |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-may-08-ca-27671-story.html |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> It earned {{USD|34.8 million|long=No}} during its opening weekend, making it the third-highest for an R-rated film, after ''[[Air Force One (film)|Air Force One]]'' ({{USD|37.1 million|long=No}}) and ''[[Interview with the Vampire (film)|Interview with the Vampire]]'' ({{USD|36.4 million|long=No}}), and the number one film of the weekend.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 9, 2000 |title=Weekend Box Office |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/article/ed2977170436/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003225246/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/article/ed2977170436/ |archive-date=October 3, 2022 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=[[Box Office Mojo]]}}</ref> The film remained number one in its second weekend, collecting {{USD|24.6 million|long=No}} and beating out newcomer ''[[Battlefield Earth (film)|Battlefield Earth]]'' ({{USD|11.5 million|long=No}}).<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 17, 2000 |title='Gladiator' muscles out competition again at theaters |url=https://www.brainerddispatch.com/newsmd/gladiator-muscles-out-competition-again-at-theaters |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=Brainerd Dispatch}}</ref> During its third weekend, ''Gladiator'' fell to second place with {{USD|19.7 million|long=No}}, behind ''[[Dinosaur (2000 film)|Dinosaur]]'' ({{USD|38.9 million|long=No}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Domestic 2000 Weekend 20 |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/weekend/2000W20/ |access-date=2022-12-23 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref> The film spent a total of ten weeks in the top ten at the box office, and was in theaters for over a year, finishing its theatrical run on May 10, 2001. Its total gross in the United States and Canada was {{USD|187.7 million|long=No}}.<ref name="GL">{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/releasegroup/gr2536067589/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref>

In the United Kingdom, ''Gladiator'' opened on May 12, 2000, and grossed £3.5 million in its opening weekend. It spent seven weeks at [[List of 2000 box office number-one films in the United Kingdom|number one]], and its total gross surpassed {{USD|43 million|long=No}}.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite magazine |date=19 May 2000 |title=International box office: UK/Ireland |magazine=[[Screen International]] |page=26}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |date=June 30, 2000 |title=International box office: UK/Ireland |magazine=[[Screen International]] |page=22}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=July 21, 2000|page=39|title=Gladiator roars past $200m internationally|last=Scott|first=Mary}}</ref>}} The film was also number one for seven weeks in Italy, and for five weeks in France.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=July 14, 2000|page=26|title=International box office: Italy}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=June 30, 2000|page=23|title=Gladiator rules in Italy|last=Senjanovic|first=Natasha}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Screen International]]|date=August 4, 2000|page=23|title=French opening boosts M:I2 worldwide gross|last=Scott|first=Mary}}</ref>}} Outside of the United States and Canada, ''Gladiator'' grossed {{USD|277.8 million|long=No}}, for a total worldwide gross of {{USD|465.5 million|long=No}} against a budget of {{USD|103 million|long=No}}.<ref name="GL" /> It was the second-highest-grossing film worldwide in 2000, behind ''[[Mission: Impossible 2]]'' ({{USD|546.3 million|long=No}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 Worldwide Box Office |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2000/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=Box Office Mojo}}</ref>

===Theatrical re-releases===
In 2020, ''Gladiator'' was re-released in Australia and the Netherlands to commemorate its 20th anniversary. This limited release grossed {{USD|4.8 million|long=No}}. The following year, it was re-released in the United Kingdom, earning a gross of {{USD|16,257|long=No}}.<ref name="GL" /> In 2024, it was released again the UK, this time earning $125,898.<ref name="GL" />

===Home media and rights===
''Gladiator'' was first released on DVD and VHS on November 21, 2000, and generated {{USD|60 million|long=No}} in sales within the first week.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hettrick |first=Scott |date=November 9, 2000 |title='Gladiator' DVD to hit U.S., U.K. |url=https://variety.com/2000/digital/features/gladiator-dvd-to-hit-u-s-u-k-1117789019/ |access-date=April 8, 2023 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web  |title=Gladiator, X-Men Set DVD Records - ABC News |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/story?id=112779&page=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091005234725/https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/story?id=112779&page=1 |archive-date=2009-10-05 |access-date=2025-06-14 |website=abcnews.go.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator (2000) - Financial Information |url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Gladiator-(2000) |access-date=2025-06-14 |website=The Numbers}}</ref>}} 

In September 2009, ''Gladiator'' was released by [[Paramount Home Entertainment]] on Blu-ray. It was re-released in August 2010 in a higher quality transfer, and in May 2018 it was released on Ultra HD Blu-ray.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator DVD Release Date |url=https://www.dvdsreleasedates.com/movies/977/Gladiator-(2000).html |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=DVDs Release Dates |language=en}}</ref> An extended version of the film, with 16 extra minutes of footage, is also available on Blu-ray, DVD and VHS.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvdcompare.net/comparisons/film.php?fid=573|title=Gladiator (2000) DVD comparison|website=DVDCompare.net|access-date=August 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvdcompare.net/comparisons/film.php?fid=15057|title=Gladiator (2000) Blu-ray comparison|website=DVDCompare.net|access-date=August 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvdcompare.net/comparisons/film.php?fid=46574|title=Gladiator (2000) 4k Blu-ray comparison|website=DVDCompare.net|access-date=August 15, 2024}}</ref>}} In March 2021, Paramount Home Entertainment included ''Gladiator'' as part of a ten-film Blu-ray set.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/review/74768|title=Best Picture Essentials 10 Movie Collection (Blu-ray + Digital)|date=March 23, 2021|website=www.dvdtalk.com|access-date=August 19, 2025}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|80|7.1|260|While not everyone will be entertained by ''Gladiator''{{'s}} glum revenge story, Russell Crowe thunderously wins the crowd with a star-making turn that provides Ridley Scott's opulent resurrection of Rome its bruised heart.|ref=yes|access-date={{RT data|access date}}}} On [[Metacritic]], the film has a score of 67 out of 100, based on 46 critics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/gladiator/ |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=Metacritic}}</ref> Audiences polled on ''Gladiator''<nowiki/>'s opening day by the market research firm [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/ |access-date=2024-02-05 |website=Cinemascore |language=en-US}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=[[WP:LINKROT]] an empty search box is not a suitable reference|date=November 2024}} 

''Gladiator'' was called "magnificent", "compelling", and "richly enjoyable" by some critics.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name="GT">{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2000 |title='GLAD' TIDINGS |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2000-05-05-0005050133-story.html |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=Chicago Tribune}}</ref><ref name="GR">{{Cite web |last=McCarthy |first=Todd |date=2000-04-24 |title=Gladiator |url=https://variety.com/2000/film/reviews/gladiator-3-1200461595/ |access-date=2024-02-05 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="NP">{{Cite news |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |date=2000-05-12 |title=No place like Rome |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2000/may/12/3 |access-date=2024-02-03 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>}} Crowe's performance in particular received praise. Writing for ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', [[Joe Morgenstern|Joe Morgensten]] said that Crowe "doesn't use tricks in this role to court our approval. He earns it the old-fashioned way, by daring to be quiet, if not silent, and intensely, implacably strong."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Morgenstern |first=Joe |date=2000-05-06 |title=Crowe Sizzles as Rome Burns in Epic 'Gladiator'; An Empire Strikes Back |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB957485792293788701 |access-date=2022-09-05 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' wrote that Crowe brings an "essential physical and psychological reality to the role", while Kirk Honeycutt of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' said that Crowe uses "his burly frame and expressive face to give dimension to what might otherwise have been comic book heroics."<ref name="IA">{{Cite web |last=Turan |first=Kenneth |date=May 5, 2000 |title=Into the Arena |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-may-05-ca-26670-story.html |access-date=February 10, 2024 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="TR">{{Cite web |last=Honeycutt |first=Kirk |date=2017-05-05 |title='Gladiator': THR's 2000 Review |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/gladiator-review-2000-movie-1000492/ |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' called Crowe's performance "simply splendid".<ref name="GR" />

Several critics also praised Scott's directing and the visual style of the film. [[Manohla Dargis]] of ''[[LA Weekly]]'' commended Scott's state-of-the-art filmmaking and expressed admiration for the film's "breathtaking, brutal lyricism".<ref name="SG">{{Cite web |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |date=May 3, 2000 |title=Saving General Maximus |url=https://www.laweekly.com/saving-general-maximus/ |access-date=February 5, 2024 |website=LA Weekly}}</ref> ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' called the opening battle sequence "extraordinary", and described Scott as a "visual artist at his most deluxe."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://ew.com/article/2000/05/05/gladiator-4/ |access-date=2024-01-28 |website=EW.com |language=en}}</ref> Michael Wilmington of ''[[Chicago Tribune|The Chicago Tribune]]'' called ''Gladiator'' "visually electrifying".<ref name="GT" /> In addition to Crowe's acting and Scott's directing, some reviewers also applauded John Mathieson's [[cinematography]], [[Arthur Max]]'s production design, and the musical score composed by Hans Zimmer and Lisa Gerrard.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name="GT" /><ref name="GR" /><ref name="NP" /><ref name="IA" /><ref name="TR" /><ref name="Gladiator">{{Cite web |last=Nathan |first=Ian |date=2000-11-05 |title=Gladiator Review |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/gladiator-review/ |access-date=2024-06-18 |website=Empire |language=en}}</ref>}}

Although critics lauded many aspects of ''Gladiator'', some derided the screenplay. Ian Nathan of ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' magazine called the dialogue "pompous", "overwritten", and "prone to plain silliness".<ref name="Gladiator" /> [[Roger Ebert]] said the script "employs depression as a substitute for personality, and believes that if characters are bitter and morose enough, we won't notice how dull they are."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ebert |first=Roger |title=Gladiator movie review & film summary (2000) {{!}} Roger Ebert |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/gladiator-2000 |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=www.rogerebert.com/ |language=en}}</ref> Manohla Dargis called the story predictable and formulaic.<ref name="SG" />

In his 2004 book ''The Assassination of Julius Caesar,'' the political scientist [[Michael Parenti]] described ''Gladiator'' as "unencumbered by any trace of artistic merit". He also criticized the film's depiction of Roman citizens, claiming that it portrays them as bloodthirsty savages.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Parenti |first=Michael |title=The Assassination of Julius Caesar |pages=8–9 |date=2004 |publisher=The New Press |isbn=9781595585561 |ol=8666786M }}</ref> Brandon Zachary of ''[[Screen Rant|ScreenRant]]'' has claimed that the plot of ''Gladiator'' borrows heavily from the 1964 film ''[[The Fall of the Roman Empire (film)|''The Fall of the Roman Empire'']]'', which is also about the transition from Marcus Aurelius to Commodus and the latter's downfall.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zachary |first1=Brandon |date=13 May 2024 |title=Gladiator Is A Secret Remake Of This 60-Year-Old Historical Epic |url=https://screenrant.com/gladiator-secret-remake-fall-roman-empire-movie/#:~:text=Gladiator%20Heavily%20Borrows%20From%20The%20Fall%20Of%20The%20Roman%20Empire&text=Both%20The%20Fall%20of%20the,doubt%20about%20his%20son%20Commodus. |access-date=30 September 2024 |website=ScreenRant |language=en}}</ref>

===Accolades===
''Gladiator'' won various awards, including the [[Academy Award for Best Picture]], the [[BAFTA Award for Best Film]] and the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama]].{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/109917846/oscar-crowe-roberts-named-best-actor/ |title=Oscar: Crowe, Roberts named best actor, actress |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220921024332/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/109917846/oscar-crowe-roberts-named-best-actor/ |date=March 26, 2001 |access-date=September 21, 2022 |archive-date=September 21, 2022 |page=6 |publisher=[[Detroit Free Press]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gladiator |url=https://goldenglobes.com/film/gladiator/ |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=Golden Globes |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 25, 2001 |title=Gladiator wins BAFTA's Best Film |url=http://www.cnn.com/2001/SHOWBIZ/Movies/02/25/baftas.winners/index.html |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=CNN}}</ref>}}

==Historical accuracy==
''Gladiator'' is loosely based on real events that occurred within the [[Roman Empire]] in the latter half of the 2nd century AD. Scott intended to portray Roman culture more accurately than previous films, so he hired several historians as advisors. Nevertheless, multiple deviations from historical accuracy were made to increase interest, maintain narrative continuity, and for practical or safety reasons. At least one historical advisor resigned due to these changes. Another asked not to be mentioned in the credits. Allen Ward, a historian at the University of Connecticut, believed that a higher level of historical accuracy would not have made ''Gladiator'' less interesting or exciting. He asserted that filmmakers must be granted some artistic license when adapting historical events, but this license should not be employed to completely disregard facts.{{sfn|Winkler|2004|p=6}}<ref>{{cite web |last=Ward |first=Allen |date=May 2001 |title=The Movie "Gladiator" in Historical Perspective |url=http://ablemedia.com/ctcweb/showcase/wardgladiator1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513100700/http://ablemedia.com/ctcweb/showcase/wardgladiator1.html |archive-date=2013-05-13 |access-date=December 8, 2010 |work=[[University of Connecticut]]}}</ref>

===Fictionalization===
A number of events in the film are presented in a way that directly contradicts historical fact.
* Marcus Aurelius was not murdered by his son Commodus, as shown in the film; he died at [[Vindobona]] (modern [[Vienna]]) in 180 AD from the [[Antonine Plague]]. The epidemic, believed to be either [[smallpox]] or [[measles]], swept through the Roman Empire during his reign.{{Sfn|Southern|2001|p=18}}
* There is no indication that Marcus Aurelius wished to return the Empire to a republican form of government, as depicted in ''Gladiator.'' Moreover, Aurelius shared the rule of the Empire with Commodus for three years before his own death. Commodus then ruled alone until his death in 192 AD.{{sfn|Grant|1997|p=95}}
* The film depicts Aurelius seizing victory in the [[Marcomannic Wars]]. In reality, the wars were ongoing when he died. Commodus secured peace with the two Germanic tribes allied against Rome, the [[Marcomanni]] and the [[Quadi]], immediately after his father's death.{{Sfn|Southern|2001|p=22}}
* The character Maximus is fictional, although in some respects he resembles [[Spartacus]], who led a slave revolt in 73-71 BCE, and [[Marcus Nonius Macrinus]], a general and friend of Marcus Aurelius.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Popham |first=Peter |title=Found: Tomb of the general who inspired 'Gladiator' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/found-tomb-of-the-general-who-inspired-gladiator-963797.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303105155/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/found-tomb-of-the-general-who-inspired-gladiator-963797.html |archive-date=March 3, 2009 |website=The Independent}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2008 |title='Gladiator' tomb is found in Rome |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7675633.stm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090322114952/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/7675633.stm |archive-date=March 22, 2009 |access-date=July 9, 2024 |website=BBC News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boom |first=Carina |date=December 6, 2012 |title=Tomb of Roman general who inspired Gladiator reburied |url=http://prehist.org/news/165/Tomb%2Bof%2BRoman%2Bgeneral%2Bwho%2Binspired%2BGladiator%2Breburied |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927115329/http://prehist.org/news/165/Tomb+of+Roman+general+who+inspired+Gladiator+reburied |archive-date=September 27, 2013 |website=PreHist}}</ref>}}
* Although Commodus engaged in show combat in the Colosseum, he was not killed in the arena; he was strangled while taking a bath by the wrestler Narcissus. Commodus reigned for over twelve years, unlike the shorter period portrayed in the film.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Commodus |encyclopedia=Encyclopædia Britannica Online |url=https://www.britannica.com/eb/article-9024967/Commodus |access-date=2008-06-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080617094833/https://www.britannica.com/eb/article-9024967/Commodus |archive-date=2008-06-17 |url-status=live}}</ref>
* In ''Gladiator'', Lucilla is depicted as the widow of Lucius Verus. She has one son, also named Lucius Verus. In reality, Lucilla's son died long before the reign of Commodus, and she remarried [[Claudius Pompeianus]] soon after Verus' death. She had been married to Claudius for 11 years by the time her brother became Emperor, and her only living son during this time was Aurelius Pompeianus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peacock |first=Phoebe B. |date=30 January 2001 |title=Lucius Verus (161-169 A.D.) |url=https://www.roman-emperors.sites.luc.edu/lverus.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328095946/http://www.roman-emperors.org/lverus.htm |archive-date=March 28, 2018 |website=Roman-Emperors.org}}</ref>
* The real-life Lucilla was implicated in a plot to assassinate her brother Commodus in 182 AD, along with several others. She was first exiled to the island of [[Capri]] by Commodus, then executed on his orders later in the year.{{sfn|Grant|1997|p=96}}
* In the film, Marcus Aurelius bans gladiatorial games in Rome. The real Aurelius, however, banned games only in [[Antioch]]. No games were ever banned in Rome.{{sfn|Winkler|2004|p=}}

===Anachronisms===
Some costumes and weapons are depicted inaccurately in ''Gladiator.''
* Although ''Gladiator'' takes place in the 2nd century AD, the [[Lorica segmentata|Imperial Gallic armor]] and the [[Imperial helmet#Imperial Gallic|helmets]] worn by the legionaries are from AD 75, a century earlier. The [[centurion]]s, [[Roman cavalry|cavalry]], [[Aquilifer|standard bearers]], and [[auxilia]]ries would have worn scale armor, known as [[lorica squamata]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=DeVries |first1=Kelly |title=Medieval Weapons: An Illustrated History of Their Impact |last2=Smith |first2=Robert Douglas |publisher=ABC-CLIO |year=2007 |isbn=978-1851095261 |pages=24–27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Scale (Lorica Squamata) |url=http://rubens.anu.edu.au/raid1/student_projects97/armour/scale/scale.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620213422/http://rubens.anu.edu.au/raid1/student_projects97/armour/scale/scale.html |archive-date=2015-06-20 |access-date=20 June 2015 |publisher=[[Australian National University]]}}</ref>
* The Praetorian Guards wear [[Tyrian purple]] in the film, but this wardrobe is not corroborated by historical evidence. On campaign, they usually wore standard legionary equipment with some unique decorative elements.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rankov |first=Boris |title=The Praetorian Guard |publisher=Osprey Publishing |year=1994 |isbn=9781855323612}}</ref>
* ''Gladiator'' depicts [[Germanic tribes]] inaccurately wearing clothing from the [[Stone Age]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Junkelmann |first=Marcus |title=Hollywoods Traum von Rom |date=December 31, 2004 |publisher=Philipp von Zabern |isbn=9783805329057 |pages=117, 120, 195}}</ref>
* The film shows the Roman cavalry using [[stirrup]]s. In reality, the cavalry used a two-horned saddle without stirrups. The stirrups were employed during filming because riding with a Roman saddle requires additional training and skill.{{sfn|Winkler|2004|p=}}
* According to the classical scholar Martin Winkler, [[catapult]]s and [[ballista]]e would not have been used in a forest, as they were reserved primarily for [[siege]]s and were rarely used in open battles.{{sfn|Winkler|2004|p=}}
* There is no documentation of the use of flaming arrows or flaming catapult canisters in ancient history.{{sfn|Winkler|2004|p=}}

== Sequels ==
{{Main|Gladiator II|l1 = ''Gladiator II''}}

A sequel to ''Gladiator'', titled ''[[Gladiator II]]'', was released in November 2024.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Huff |first=Lauren |date=April 11, 2024 |title=Everything we know about 'Gladiator II' so far |url=https://ew.com/movies/gladiator-2-everything-we-know/ |access-date=2024-04-15 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |language=en}}</ref> It is directed by Ridley Scott, written by [[David Scarpa]], and produced by [[Scott Free Productions]] for [[Paramount Pictures]]. It stars [[Paul Mescal]], [[Denzel Washington]], [[Joseph Quinn]], [[Fred Hechinger]], [[Pedro Pascal]], Connie Nielsen, and Derek Jacobi, the last two reprising their roles from ''Gladiator''. In addition to directing the film, Scott served as a producer alongside Michael Pruss, Douglas Wick and [[Lucy Fisher]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kroll |first=Justin |date=2023-01-06 |title=Paul Mescal To Star In Ridley Scott's 'Gladiator' Sequel For Paramount |url=https://deadline.com/2023/01/gladiator-2-star-paul-mescal-ridley-scott-paramount-1235212512/ |access-date=2024-02-12 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> The costume designer [[Janty Yates]] and the production designer Arthur Max—both of whom worked on ''Gladiator''—returned for the sequel.<ref>{{cite web |author=Matt Villei |date=January 6, 2023 |title=Ridley Scott's 'Gladiator' Sequel Casts 'Normal People's Paul Mescal as Lead |url=https://collider.com/gladiator-2-cast-paul-mescal/ |access-date=January 6, 2023 |website=Collider}}</ref> The story of the film centers on Lucilla's son, Lucius, who is now a grown man and is revealed to be the son of Maximus.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Huff |first=Lauren |date=September 23, 2024 |title=Gladiator II trailer reveals that Lucius is the son of Russell Crowe's Maximus after all |url=https://ew.com/gladiator-2-trailer-reveals-lucius-son-russell-crowe-maximus-8715524 |accessdate=September 23, 2024 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=February 3, 2023 |title='Gladiator 2′ Gets Pre-Thanksgiving 2024 Release |url=https://deadline.com/2023/02/gladiator-2-release-date-1235249039/ |access-date=February 3, 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> A third film is also in the works.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite news |date=23 November 2024 |title=Everything Ridley Scott Has Said About 'Gladiator III' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/everything-ridley-scott-has-said-gladiator-3-1236069492/ |access-date=25 November 2024 |publisher=hollywoodreporter.com |agency=hollywoodreporter.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=8 November 2024 |title=Godfather-style Gladiator 3 already in the works, hints Sir Ridley Scott |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2024/11/08/godfather-style-gladiator-3-in-the-works-sir-ridley-scott/?msockid=31a9748abec86af4251361c8bf7c6b63 |access-date=25 November 2024
